chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah and Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah, who said: Zakariyya ibn Adam asked him about what the cheetah and the dog kill.

He said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: 'The dog and the cheetah are equal. If it catches its prey and holds it and dies while it is with it, then eat it, for it held it for you. And if it catches it and eats from it, then do not eat from it, for it only held it for itself.'
And the game of the dog, when it is out of sight, its eating is not permissible if it dies.

key_terms.أَمْسَكَ: Held or restrained (referring to holding the prey)
key_terms.الْأَفْهَدُ: Cheetah (a type of wild cat used for hunting)
key_terms.الْكَلْبُ: Dog (specifically hunting dog in this context)
key_terms.غَابَ عَنِ الْعَيْنِ: Out of sight (referring to the prey being hidden from the hunter's view)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating game killed by a hunting dog or cheetah in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that dogs and cheetahes are legally equivalent in hunting, with permissibility hinging on whether the animal retains the prey for the hunter or consumes it for itself. This ruling is further refined by the condition that the prey must be within the hunter's sight to ensure the kill is intentional and valid. The hadith underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the hunter's control and intent in determining the ritual purity and permissibility of the meat.
